title: Sending a channel reply fails with unrecognized broadcast key
summary: The owner reported that sending a channel reply failed because the request included an unrecognized 'broadcast' key. A later committed fix removes the owner-facing broadcast option and rejects broadcast:true explicitly, so this specific client/server mismatch is resolved. The named root was the only post available in the saved input; channel_read(threadId) returned no replies. No matching active Task was found; the related channel broadcast change was an owner direction recorded in the commit and thread-view spec.
nextAction: None for the reported error. If it recurs, capture the current client/server version and request payload; the repository has a regression test for rejecting broadcast:true and accepting normal thread replies.
evidence: agent_notes/2026-10-05_channel-thread-audit/inputs/post_01a0e8be-2685-7011-aaa6-f8365111700b.json records the exact owner error and root post.
Commit ef328383f5260812951b95b490d48c5409455f62 (Remove channel broadcast option from owner replies) is an ancestor of current HEAD b39dca3651024f9a8ffcd4c3b87853ab0d7c90ba.

At HEAD, server/src/buddies/routes.ts schema uses broadcast: z.literal(false).default(false), and server/test/buddies-v2.test.ts contains 'owner channel replies stay in threads and reject old broadcast requests' (asserts broadcast:true returns 400, normal reply returns 201).
Commit ef32838 also removes the composer checkbox and omits broadcast from new reply requests.
limitations: Live send was not exercised; no tests were run per instruction.
Working tree is dirty with unrelated files, so verification is against committed HEAD source plus ancestor history, not a clean tree.
Buddy channel_read returned an empty post list for the requested thread; replies could not be independently fetched or paginated.
